'''''Acquacotta''''' ({{IPA|it|ˌakkwaˈkɔtta|lang}}; {{literally|cooked water}}) is an [[Italian cuisine|Italian]] [[broth]]-based [[bread soup]] that was originally a [[peasant food]]. Its preparation and consumption dates back to ancient history, and it originated in the coastal area known as the [[Maremma]], in southern [[Tuscany]] and northern [[Lazio]]. The dish was invented in part as a means to make hardened, stale bread edible. In contemporary times, ingredients can vary, and additional ingredients are sometimes used. Variations of the dish include ''acquacotta con funghi'' and ''acquacotta con peperoni''.
